canonical_statement: Every real-valued discrete-time martingale on a finite measure space that is bounded in L^p for an exponent 1 < p < infinity converges almost surely and in L^p to the same L^p random variable.
domain_and_universes: universe u; Omega : Type u; MeasurableSpace Omega; a finite Measure Omega; Nat-indexed, Real-valued process; exponent : ENNReal; Prop in Lean universe 0
hypotheses: there is bound : NNReal with eLpNorm (D.process n) D.exponent D.measure <= bound for every n
conclusion: There exists limit : Omega -> Real which is MemLp at the same exponent and measure, D.process n tends pointwise to limit almost everywhere, and the eLpNorm of D.process n - limit tends to zero.

degenerate_cases: The finite measure may be zero and the measurable space arbitrary. No probability normalization is imposed. The strict inequalities kernel-check exclusion of p = 1 and p = infinity. Continuous time, p <= 1, p = infinity, and Banach-valued processes are outside this target.
